t.1.48.1: Śaunaka said: At the snake sacrifice of the wise king Janamejaya, the descendant of the Pāṇḍavas, who then were the officiating priests, the supreme seers?
t.1.48.2: And who were the sadasyas at that most dreadful snake sacrifice, which caused the serpents excessive despair and was a great terror to them?
t.1.48.3: Dear son, you should tell all of this in detail, for those who were versed in the procedure of the snake sacrifice ought to be known, O son of the sūta.
t.1.48.4: Sūta said: Well then, I shall tell you here the names of the wise men who were the officiating priests and the members of the assembly of that king at that time.
t.1.48.5: Then the hotṛ priest there was the brahmin Caṇḍabhārgava, born in the lineage of Cyavana, renowned as the best of those who know the Veda.
t.1.48.6: The udgātṛ was the aged and learned brāhmaṇa, the noble Kautsa Jaimini; Śārṅgarava became the brahman priest, and Bodhapiṅgala the adhvaryu.
t.1.48.8: Asita and Devala, as well as Nārada and Parvata, Ātreya, Kuṇḍajaṭhara, and likewise the twice-born Kuṭighaṭa.
t.1.48.7: Vyāsa, accompanied by his sons and disciples, became a member of the sacrificial assembly, and so did Uddālaka, Śamaṭhaka, and Śvetaketu as the fifth.
t.1.48.10: These and many other brāhmaṇas of rigorous vows were the assessors there at the sacrificial session of Pārikṣita.
t.1.48.9: Vātsya, the aged Śrutaśravas, devoted to austerity and Vedic study, Kahoḍa, Devaśarman, Maudgalya and Śamasaubhara were also among them.
t.1.48.11: Then, as the officiating priests poured oblations into the fire at that great rite, the snake sacrifice, terrible serpents fell there, bringing dread to all living beings.
t.1.48.12: Streams carrying the fat and marrow of the nāgas were set flowing, and then a dreadful stench blew forth from those who were burning without cease.
t.1.48.13: And unceasingly there was heard the clamor of the Nāgas as they fell, and likewise of those stationed in the sky, as they were fiercely roasted by the fire.
t.1.48.14: But Takṣaka, that lord of serpents, as soon as he heard that King Janamejaya had been consecrated for the sacrifice, went to the abode of Puraṃdara.
t.1.48.15: Then the best of serpents, having related everything just as it had happened, frightened, having committed an offence, went for refuge to Puraṃdara.
t.1.48.16: Indra, well pleased, said to him: "Here, O Takṣaka, lord of the Nāgas, there is no fear for you in any way from that snake sacrifice."
t.1.48.17: Long ago, for your sake, I won the favor of the Grandsire; therefore there is no danger for you. Let the fever of your mind depart.
t.1.48.18: Thus reassured by him, that best of serpents then dwelt there in the abode of Śakra, joyful and happy.
t.1.48.19: As the Nāgas fell ceaselessly into the fire, Vāsuki, deeply distressed, his retinue reduced to a small remnant, was tormented with grief.
t.1.48.20: A dreadful faintness entered Vāsuki, the lord of serpents, and he, his heart reeling, spoke these words to his sister.
t.1.48.21: My limbs are burning, good lady, and the directions no longer appear clearly to me; I seem to sink down in bewilderment, and my mind seems to whirl.
t.1.48.22: My sight whirls exceedingly, and my heart seems to be bursting; today I shall fall helplessly into that blazing fire.
t.1.48.23: That sacrifice of Pārikṣita is under way with the desire to kill us. Clearly I too must go to the abode of the king of the ancestors.
t.1.48.24: This is the time that has now arrived, my sister, for whose sake you were given long ago to Jaratkāru; so save us together with our kinsmen.
t.1.48.26: Therefore, dear child, speak today to your own son, the boy esteemed by the elders and foremost among knowers of the Veda, for the deliverance of me together with my dependents.
t.1.48.25: Āstīka, it is said, will put a stop to that sacrifice once it is underway, O best of serpent-women; the Grandfather himself told me so long ago.
